Karthik / Laura — forwarding Leah's report. TL;DR: Aurelia is on a reserved tranche but we appear to be oversubscribed by concurrent demand pattern mismatches across customers who share that tranche window. Options:

- A: Temporary slice reallocation (move Aurelia to a higher share for 08:00-11:00 ET for the next 10 business days). Fast but reduces capacity available for other customers who signed in to the same tranche.
- B: Short-term vertical scale (spin up 2 additional GPUs attached to tranche for 2 hours daily) — more cost, longer infra ops time, preserves fairness.
- C: SLA amendment + credits (formalize redundancy window and give them credit for incidents while we schedule long-term capacity).

I've sketched an allocation plan and what this buys in terms of headroom — see allocation_plan_v1.xlsx attached. Need guidance on whether we have authority to modify tranche shares for a customer mid-contract, or whether this needs leadership sign-off (legal also involved if we change SLA).

Can we review options and tradeoffs in a quick sync?

Thanks — dug into the telemetry. Key facts:
- The tranche is oversubscribed during 08:00-10:30 ET by two customers (Aurelia + third-party pilot). The third-party load is burstier and not covered by tighter request-shaping.
- Our autoscaler has been reluctant to scale because the allocation is configured as "slice-shared" (soft isolation).
- Spinning GPUs is feasible but will take ~18-24 hours to provision and warm KV caches; not good for same-day remediation.

Suggested path: immediate short-term mitigation = implement request shaping and limit concurrent streams for the third-party pilot for the next 72 hours + bump Aurelia's slice share to +20% during 08:00-10:30 ET for ten business days while we coordinate a longer-term tranche split. This preserves fairness by applying policy to the noisy actor.

Policy/legal note: changing slice shares mid-contract is allowed under our T&Cs if both parties agree or if a critical SLA breach is imminent — but it must go through ops and legal. If legal wants credits instead of a share change we should quantify the cost and seconds of latency for Aurelia.

Options summarized in the attached allocation_plan_v1.xlsx.

Appreciate the packet and the plan. I authorize a temporary tranche reallocation in favor of Aurelia for the morning window under these guardrails:

1) Reallocate +20% slice share to Aurelia for 08:00-10:30 ET for ten business days, effective immediately. Ops to log the change and monitor headroom metrics.
2) Apply request-shaping limit to the noisy third-party pilot for the same window; include an automated throttle policy flagged in case error rate improves.
3) Offer Aurelia a one-time credit equivalent to 5% of July committed spend, conditioned on outage confirmation in the report and acceptance of a short SLA addendum that formalizes the morning tranche guarantee. Legal to review the addendum — attach proposed_sla_addendum_v2.pdf.

This is an operational exception; keep the execs briefed. Rishi

What we did (short term):
- Increased your morning slice share by +20% for 08:00-10:30 ET, active now through 2026-08-13 (ten business days).
- Applied targeted request shaping to the third-party pilot that was driving bursty concurrency; we will automatically relax the throttle if downstream error behavior normalizes.
- Issued a one-time account credit equal to 5% of July committed spend (pending legal/finance confirmation).

What we need from you:
- Review the proposed SLA addendum attached (proposed_sla_addendum_v2.pdf) and confirm acceptance or mark edits by EOD 2026-08-03 so legal can finalize.
- If you see residual tail latency, please send packet captures/IDs and we'll keep priority triage open.

Longer-term: we're scheduling a tranche split to give Aurelia a dedicated morning slice; provisioning ETA is ~2 weeks (dependent on capacity availability). We'll share the tranche split schedule and cost/commitment options early next week.

Thanks again — we'll monitor closely and follow up with the tranche split plan.

—Ben
